gaps.sentence: The window has ___ been repaired, I'm glad to say.
gaps.explanation: 'Has since been repaired' = between that time and now.

gaps.sentence: I'm looking forward to ___ you next week.
gaps.explanation: 'to' is a preposition here, so -ing follows.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, we ___ have finished the whole report.
gaps.explanation: 'By + future time' calls for the future perfect: will have finished.

gaps.sentence: ___ from being annoyed, she was delighted.
gaps.explanation: 'far from + adjective' = not at all: Far from being annoyed…

gaps.sentence: We stopped ___ some photos on the way.
gaps.explanation: 'stop to do' = pause in order to do something.

gaps.sentence: The witnesses gave accounts that contradicted one ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Contradict one another' is the reciprocal form used for more than two people.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ you, I'd apologise immediately.
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' — subjunctive 'were' for unreal situations.

gaps.sentence: The findings will be published in ___ course.
gaps.hint: in ___ course = at the right time
gaps.explanation: 'In due course' = eventually, when the time is right.
